source.title: Enhancing Sharpness-Aware Minimization by Learning Perturbation Radius
source.authors: Xuehao Wang; Weisen Jiang; Shuai Fu; Yu Zhang

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendices. Some plotted figure text is garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training–test generalization gaps and qualitative loss-landscape flatness for SAM variants, using a learned perturbation radius. It does not test the claim versions’ specific conditions or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The study reports that LETS-SAM and LETS-ASAM have smaller generalization gaps than their SAM and ASAM counterparts near convergence on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and describes their loss landscapes as flatter. Gap values are presented only in figures; no precise values are recoverable from the text. It also reports accuracy and other benchmark results, but these compare the study’s proposed methods and do not directly test a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop and benchmark LETS-SAM and LETS-ASAM. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare generalization-measure rankings. Qualitative loss surfaces and smaller loss gaps do not test that version. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is faithful: the authors conclude that LETS learns perturbation radii and improves SAM and ASAM benchmark performance across the tested tasks and architectures. They additionally report smaller loss generalization gaps near convergence and qualitatively flatter loss landscapes.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes LETS, a bilevel method that learns the SAM perturbation radius from training and validation losses, and compares it with SAM and ASAM.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation radius ρ substantially affects SAM/ASAM accuracy; LETS performance is reported as not very sensitive to initialization over ρ0 ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2}.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 4.1 and D.3 report smaller test-minus-training loss gaps near convergence for LETS-SAM and LETS-ASAM than their respective baselines across three convolutional architectures on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Numerical differences cannot be recovered from the supplied plots.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning SAM's perturbation radius can reduce the loss generalization gap near convergence in these tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 4.7 and D.4 describe flatter loss surfaces for LETS variants on ResNet-18, using two orthogonal weight-perturbation directions. They provide no magnitude-aware tolerance statistic or generalization-measure ranking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LETS variants produce qualitatively flatter plotted loss surfaces than their SAM or ASAM baselines on ResNet-18 for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

record.problems: Generalization-gap comparisons are figure-only; the supplied figure text is garbled, so no numerical gap sizes can be extracted. Validation mini-batches are randomly sampled from the training set for the CIFAR experiments, as stated by the authors.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for accuracy tables or the qualitative loss-landscape figures: those report comparisons of the proposed method’s benchmark performance or visualizations, not a listed version’s named outcome. No numerical values can be recovered from the gap figures.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training, near-perfect random-label fit, and held-out accuracy under both conditions. Partial label-noise robustness experiments do not establish these.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under matched tuning regimes. Using different optimizers for different workloads supplies no such comparison.
Large versus small batches within a workload under fixed epoch budgets, with or without recipe adaptation.
Controlled dropout effects on held-out error. Listed dropout settings and tuning ranges are not outcome comparisons.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The study instead reports qualitative two-direction loss surfaces and test-minus-training loss gaps.
Removal of examples selected by label memorization versus matched random removal, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the text does explicitly report the direction of the loss-gap comparisons. Qualitative landscapes and benchmark tables are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label test performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The study reports qualitative loss-landscape comparisons but does not test the specified measure or its ranking.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained; training stage not otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared LETS-SAM generalization gap with SAM during training.
rows.measure: Generalization gap, defined as test loss minus training loss.
rows.value: LETS-SAM: figure only; text says the gap is smaller than SAM near convergence.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the comparison; the plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied figure text.
rows.check: Method-performance comparison, not a listed claim test. The stated smaller loss gap is supported by Section 4.1, but cannot establish V7's sharpness–gap relationship.
